style: Comprehensive meaningful blend (interpretive text) + amplified study form; bare transliterations in amp with Strong's carried in notes; em-dashes used sparingly; transliterations ASCII-normalized relative to the lexicon's spellings; 'the LORD' for YHWH; deity pronouns capitalized.
chapterNote: The last psalm of the Egyptian Hallel (113-118) -- almost certainly the hymn Jesus sang with the Twelve before walking out to Gethsemane (Matthew 26:30) -- and Luther's favorite, his 'own beloved psalm.' It is built as a procession. It opens and closes on the same refrain, with Israel, the priests, and the God-fearers each summoned in turn to say it: His covenant love endures forever. The middle is one man's battle testimony: called from the tight place and answered with open room; the LORD for me, so what can man do; surrounded by nations like swarming bees that go out like a thorn-fire; pushed hard to fall, but helped; chastened severely, but not handed to death -- I shall not die but live, and recount the deeds of the LORD. Then the procession reaches the temple: open to me the gates of righteousness -- and at the gate stands the psalm's immortal center, the verse Jesus applied to Himself in Jerusalem's last week and the apostles preached to its rulers: the stone the builders rejected has become the cornerstone; this is the LORD's doing, marvelous in our eyes. This is the day the LORD has made. 'Save now' -- Hosanna -- and 'Blessed is he who comes in the name of the LORD' are both here, the very words the crowds sang on Palm Sunday, and the words Jesus said Jerusalem would not hear again until she says them to Him.

1.text: Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His covenant love endures forever.
1.amp: O give thanks [yadah] unto the LORD [YHWH]; for He is good [tov]: because His mercy [chesed -- covenant love] endures for ever [olam].
1.notes: The refrain of refrains -- Israel's most-sung sentence (cf. Psalm 100:5; 136), the one the choirs sang as the temple's glory descended (cf. 2 Chronicles 5:13). tov in His character, chesed le-olam (H2617, H5769) in His commitment: the frame the whole psalm hangs inside.

2.text: Let Israel say it now: 'His covenant love endures forever.'
2.amp: Let Israel [Yisrael] now say [amar], that His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
2.notes: The first ring of the antiphon: the nation itself. na, 'now' -- the refrain is not archive material; each generation is summoned to say it fresh, in its own present tense.

3.text: Let the house of Aaron say it now: 'His covenant love endures forever.'
3.amp: Let the house [bayith] of Aaron [Aharon] now say [amar], that His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
3.notes: The second ring: the priests -- the bet Aharon (H175), the men who handle holy things daily and could grow numb to them, ordered to say the wonder aloud like everyone else.

4.text: Let those who fear the LORD say it now: 'His covenant love endures forever.'
4.amp: Let them now that fear [yare] the LORD [YHWH] say [amar], that His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
4.notes: The third ring reaches past bloodline: the yire YHWH (H3373), the God-fearers -- the Psalter's open category that Gentile converts walked into (cf. Psalm 115:11-13; Acts 13:26). Three circles, one sentence: covenant love confessed in stereo.

5.text: Out of the tight place I called on the LORD; the LORD answered me and set me in the wide open.
5.amp: I called [qara] upon the LORD [Yah] in distress ['out of distress', metsar, the KJV margin -- the tight, narrow place]: the LORD [Yah] answered [anah] me, and set me in a large place [merchab -- the broad, open room].
5.notes: The testimony's geometry: min ha-metsar (H4712), from the narrows -- distress as a canyon squeezing shut -- to the merchab (H4800), the wide room of Psalm 18:19. Prayer is the passage between the two, and Yah (H3050), the short strong form of the Name, guards both ends.

6.text: The LORD is for me; I will not be afraid. What can man do to me?
6.amp: The LORD [YHWH] is on my side ['for me', li, the KJV margin]; I will not fear [yare]: what can man [adam] do [asah] unto me?
6.notes: YHWH li -- 'the LORD is FOR me': two Hebrew words that empty fear's whole arsenal. Hebrews hands this verse to every believer facing loss (cf. Hebrews 13:6), and Paul's echo is its full flower: if God is for us, who can be against us (cf. Romans 8:31)?

7.text: The LORD is for me, among those who help me; so I will look in calm triumph on those who hate me.
7.amp: The LORD [YHWH] takes my part with them that help [azar] me: therefore shall I see [raah] my desire upon them that hate [sane] me.
7.notes: God listed in the ranks of the ozerim (H5826), the helpers -- the Almighty enrolled on the muster sheet. The 'seeing' (raah, H7200) is the survivor's steady look at a threat that spent itself: vindication as vision, not vengeance.

8.text: Better to take refuge in the LORD than to put your confidence in man.
8.amp: It is better [tov] to trust [chasah -- take refuge] in the LORD [YHWH] than to put confidence [batach] in man [adam].
8.notes: By the traditional verse-count this is the middle verse of the whole Bible -- and fittingly it weighs the two trusts: chasah (H2620) in YHWH against batach in adam. The comparative is gentle irony; one of these shelters is made of the same failing material as the man hiding in it.

9.text: Better to take refuge in the LORD than to put your confidence in princes.
9.amp: It is better [tov] to trust [chasah] in the LORD [YHWH] than to put confidence [batach] in princes [nadib -- nobles].
9.notes: The ladder's top rung tested too: nedibim (H5081), the nobles with real resources -- and the verdict unchanged. Power scales; reliability does not (cf. Psalm 146:3). The refuge-word repeats because the choice repeats daily.

10.text: All the nations surrounded me; in the name of the LORD I cut them down.
10.amp: All nations [goy] compassed me about [savav]: but in the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH] will I destroy ['cut them off', mul, the KJV margin] them.
10.notes: The battle memory begins: kol goyim (H1471), encircled by everyone at once. The cutting-verb mul (H4135) is, strikingly, the circumcision-verb -- the covenant's own blade-word: the threat trimmed away be-shem YHWH, in the Name, the only weapon named.

11.text: They surrounded me -- yes, surrounded me on every side; in the name of the LORD I cut them down.
11.amp: They compassed me about [savav]; yea, they compassed me about: but in the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH] I will destroy [mul] them.
11.notes: savav doubled (H5437): the encirclement told twice because it closed twice -- memory still feels the ring tighten. The answer does not escalate; the shem was sufficient the first time and the second.

12.text: They swarmed around me like bees, but they went out like a fire in thorns; in the name of the LORD I cut them down.
12.amp: They compassed me about [savav] like bees [deborah]; they are quenched [daak -- extinguished] as the fire [esh] of thorns [qots]: for in the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH] I will destroy [mul] them.
12.notes: Two similes for fury without staying power: the deborah-swarm (H1682) -- loud, stinging, everywhere -- and the thorn-fire of Ecclesiastes 7:6, all crackle and gone. daak (H1846), snuffed out: the siege that felt endless proved combustible.

13.text: I was pushed hard, shoved to make me fall -- but the LORD helped me.
13.amp: You have thrust sore [dachah dachah -- pushed and pushed] at me that I might fall [naphal]: but the LORD [YHWH] helped [azar] me.
13.notes: The verb doubles like the shoving it describes: dachoh dechitani (H1760), pushed and pushed again, addressed to the enemy directly -- and then the shortest turning-clause in the psalm: va-YHWH azarani, but the LORD helped me. The whole gospel of the tight place in four words.

14.text: The LORD is my strength and my song, and He has become my salvation.
14.amp: The LORD [Yah] is my strength [oz] and song [zimrah], and is become my salvation [yeshuah].
14.notes: Moses' line from the far shore of the Red Sea, quoted exactly (cf. Exodus 15:2; Isaiah 12:2): ozzi ve-zimrat Yah. Strength for the fight, song for the deliverance, and yeshuah (H3444) -- the salvation-word that is the Name of Jesus in seed form -- as the settled outcome.

15.text: The voice of ringing joy and salvation is in the tents of the righteous: 'The right hand of the LORD does valiantly!
15.amp: The voice [qol] of rejoicing [rinnah -- ringing cries] and salvation [yeshuah] is in the tabernacles [ohel -- the tents] of the righteous [tsaddiq]: the right hand [yamin] of the LORD [YHWH] does [asah] valiantly [chayil].
15.notes: The camp after the battle: rinnah (H7440) ringing tent to tent among the tsaddiqim. Their song has one subject -- the yamin YHWH (H3225), the right hand -- and one adverb: chayil (H2428), valiantly; the victory hymn credits no other arm.

16.text: The right hand of the LORD is lifted high; the right hand of the LORD does valiantly!'
16.amp: The right hand [yamin] of the LORD [YHWH] is exalted [rum]: the right hand of the LORD does [asah] valiantly [chayil].
16.notes: The tent-song's second stanza lifts the same hand higher: romemah (H7426), exalted -- raised the way a victor's arm is raised. Three yamin-clauses in two verses: the camp cannot stop looking at the hand that won.

17.text: I shall not die -- I shall live, and recount the deeds of the LORD.
17.amp: I shall not die [muth], but live [chayah], and declare [saphar -- recount] the works [maaseh] of the LORD [Yah].
17.notes: Luther wrote this verse on his study wall at Coburg while the Reformation hung in the balance: lo amut ki echyeh. Survival with a purpose clause -- chayah (H2421) in order to saphar (H5608): the spared life becomes a telling life.

18.text: The LORD has disciplined me severely, but He did not hand me over to death.
18.amp: The LORD [Yah] has chastened me sore [yasar yasar -- disciplined me with discipline]: but He has not given me over [natan] unto death [mavet].
18.notes: The doubled discipline-verb (H3256): yassor yisserani -- chastening at full strength, owned as Yah's own work, not the enemy's. But the sentence had a boundary: lo netanani la-mavet. Fatherly discipline stops short of destruction, always (cf. Hebrews 12:6, 10-11; 2 Corinthians 6:9).

19.text: Open to me the gates of righteousness; I will enter through them and give thanks to the LORD.
19.amp: Open [pathach] to me the gates [shaar] of righteousness [tsedek]: I will go [bo] into them, and I will praise [yadah] the LORD [Yah]:
19.notes: The procession arrives: the delivered man at the temple gates, the shaare tsedek (H8179, H6664), asking entrance for one purpose -- yadah (H3034), thanksgiving. Deliverance that does not walk itself to worship is only half finished.

20.text: This is the LORD's own gate; the righteous enter in through it.
20.amp: This gate [shaar] of the LORD [YHWH], into which the righteous [tsaddiq] shall enter [bo].
20.notes: The gatekeeper's answer (cf. Psalm 24:3-4): the shaar belongs to YHWH, and the tsaddiqim pass. Jesus stood in these gate-liturgies and called Himself the door itself (cf. John 10:9) -- the entrance the psalm is circling draws near.

21.text: I give You thanks, for You answered me, and You have become my salvation.
21.amp: I will praise [yadah] You: for You have heard [anah -- answered] me, and are become my salvation [yeshuah].
21.notes: Inside the gate, the vow is paid immediately: the anah of verse 5 acknowledged, and verse 14's refrain made personal address -- va-tehi li li-yeshuah, You Yourself have become my salvation. Not sent it; become it.

22.text: The stone the builders rejected has become the head of the corner.
22.amp: The stone [even] which the builders [banah] refused [maas -- rejected, despised] is become the head [rosh] stone of the corner [pinnah -- the cornerstone].
22.notes: The psalm's immortal center: the even (H68) the professionals maas (H3988), examined and discarded, now the rosh pinnah (H7218, H6438) the whole building squares to. Jesus quoted it of Himself to the temple's own builders in His last week (cf. Matthew 21:42), Peter preached it to the Sanhedrin (cf. Acts 4:11), and on it the church stands (cf. Ephesians 2:20; 1 Peter 2:6-7).

23.text: This is from the LORD Himself; it is marvelous in our eyes.
23.amp: This is the LORD'S doing ['from the LORD', me-et YHWH, the KJV margin]; it is marvellous [pala] in our eyes [ayin].
23.notes: The reversal has one author: me-et YHWH, from the LORD -- no committee reconsidered the stone; God overruled the builders. pala (H6381), the miracle-word: the rejected-exalted pattern is His signature move, and the empty tomb is its boldest stroke.

24.text: This is the day the LORD has made; in it let us rejoice and be glad.
24.amp: This is the day [yom] which the LORD [YHWH] has made [asah]; we will rejoice [gil] and be glad [samach] in it.
24.notes: In context, 'the day' is the day the Stone was vindicated -- which is why the church has sung this verse on resurrection morning from the beginning. gil and samach (H1523, H8055): joy commanded as the fitting response to a day God manufactured on purpose.

25.text: Save now, we plead with You, O LORD! O LORD, we plead -- send prosperity and success now!
25.amp: Save [yasha] now, I beseech [anna -- oh, please!] You, O LORD [YHWH]: O LORD, I beseech You, send now prosperity [tsalach -- success].
25.notes: hoshia-na (H3467, H577) -- 'save, please, now' -- the very syllables that became HOSANNA, waved with palm branches at the King riding in (cf. Matthew 21:9; John 12:13). The crowd was singing this psalm at Jesus; the psalm had been waiting for Him.

26.text: Blessed is he who comes in the name of the LORD! We bless all of you from the house of the LORD.
26.amp: Blessed [barak] be he that comes [bo] in the name [shem] of the LORD [YHWH]: we have blessed [barak] you out of the house [bayith] of the LORD.
26.notes: The gate-blessing on the arriving pilgrim -- and the verse Jesus made messianic and conditional in one breath: 'you will not see Me again UNTIL you say, Blessed is He who comes in the name of the LORD' (cf. Matthew 23:39; Luke 13:35). Jerusalem's next sight of her King waits on this sentence.

27.text: The LORD is God, and He has flooded us with light. Bind the festal sacrifice with cords, up to the horns of the altar.
27.amp: God [El] is the LORD [YHWH], which has shown us light [or]: bind [asar] the sacrifice [chag -- the festal offering] with cords [avoth], even unto the horns [qeren] of the altar [mizbeach].
27.notes: The procession's final act: light given, so a chag (H2282) -- the feast-sacrifice -- led forward, asar (H631) with avoth (H5688), the braided cords, to the qeren mizbeach (H7161, H4196). Read on the far side of the gospel, the picture stills the breath: the willing Offering bound and brought to the horns of the altar in the very week this psalm was sung to Him.

28.text: You are my God, and I will give You thanks; You are my God -- I will lift You high.
28.amp: You are my God [El], and I will praise [yadah] You: You are my God [Elohim], I will exalt [rum] You.
28.notes: The whole liturgy lands on the possessive: Eli attah -- MY God -- said twice, once as El and once as Elohim, thanksgiving and exaltation as the two hands of the same grip. The psalm's public procession ends in first-person covenant.

29.text: Give thanks to the LORD, for He is good; His covenant love endures forever.
29.amp: O give thanks [yadah] unto the LORD [YHWH]; for He is good [tov]: for His mercy [chesed] endures for ever [olam].
29.notes: The frame closes exactly where it opened -- but the refrain returns loaded with everything between: the tight place, the bees, the discipline, the Stone, the hosanna, the bound sacrifice. chesed le-olam has been demonstrated, not merely declared. If this was the hymn's last verse on Thursday night, these were among the final words Jesus sang before Gethsemane.
